query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing the soft-inducing noble metal (Pd/Pt) with aluminum in an equiatomic FeCoNi high-entropy alloy will increase its coercivity.
generation.material_initial_state: A FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy synthesized with Pd or Pt (e.g., FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt) exhibiting soft ferromagnetism and an fcc structure.
generation.intervention: Substitute Pd/Pt with Al to form an equiatomic FeCoNiAl alloy while maintaining a high configurational entropy (≥1.0R).
generation.conditions: Prepare the alloy via arc-melting under an inert atmosphere followed by high-temperature homogenization annealing to ensure complete mixing and a single-phase fcc structure; target nearly equiatomic composition to preserve high entropy.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced lattice distortion and a more pronounced magnetocrystalline anisotropy due to the introduction of Al.
generation.mechanism: Aluminum has a smaller atomic radius and different electronic effects compared to Pd/Pt, promoting lattice strain and increasing magnetocrystalline anisotropy. This, in turn, enhances domain wall pinning, resulting in significantly higher coercivity in the FeCoNiAl alloy relative to the Pd/Pt-containing baseline.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FeCoNiAl alloy will exhibit a coercivity that is measurably higher than that of the prior FeCoNiPd/Pt alloys, while maintaining a high saturation magnetization characteristic of the FeCoNi base system.
generation.baseline: FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt high-entropy alloys synthesized under similar conditions.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected to hold under synthesis conditions that promote a single fcc phase and near-equiatomic composition; deviations that lead to secondary phase formation or significant changes in configurational entropy may alter the outcome.
generation.uncertainty: The precise magnitude of the coercivity increase is uncertain and may depend on processing details (e.g., annealing temperature and time). Secondary phase formation and microstructural variations could also influence magnetic properties.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize an equiatomic FeCoNiAl high-entropy alloy using arc-melting followed by homogenization annealing under an inert atmosphere at high temperature. Prepare a control sample of FeCoNiPd (or FeCoNiPt) using identical synthesis conditions. Characterize both samples to confirm a single-phase fcc structure and measure their magnetic hysteresis loops at room temperature.
measurements: Structural phase analysis (XRD) to confirm single-phase fcc structure.
Magnetic hysteresis measurements (using VSM or SQUID) to determine coercivity (Hc) and saturation magnetization (Ms) for both samples.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercivity of the FeCoNiAl alloy is not significantly higher than that of the control FeCoNiPd/Pt alloy (under identical processing conditions), or if the alloy develops secondary phases that alter the magnetic properties, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: While the combination of saturation magnetization and coercivity for these RTA‐ treated FeCoNiMnCu films is impressive in comparison to previously reported bulk systems, the coercivity is still modest, due to the high symmetry of the cubic lattice which limits the intrinsic magnetocrystalline anisotropy. The facilitation of low‐symmetry chemical order and crystal structure combined with strong spin‐orbit coupling is in general necessary to realize strong magnetocrysalline anisotropy. To achieve these conditions in a high entropy system, we have added 50 at.% Pt to the FeCoNiMnCu alloy, employing the high entropy intermetallic design approach in search of highly anisotropic L10 ordering. Although the certainty of Pt sites reduces the configurational entropy compared to the equiatomic case, we demonstrate below that such optimized entropy can still stabilize a single high‐entropy L10 phase.

The saturation magnetization of the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi HEA reduces by more than 50% compared to samples with no Cr (AlCoFeNi). It has been previously reported earlier that MS falls linearly with increasing Cr content,,. This is mainly due to the antiferromagnetic nature of Cr. Additionally, the coercivity of the Cr containing alloy was higher than the alloy with no Cr. The MS and HC of AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi decreases with increasing annealing temperature. It has been previously reported that magnetic hardening of Fe–Co–Cr alloys is associated with the formation of a two-phase microstructure at the nanometer scale; firstly, the Fe–Co rich ferromagnetic phase, and secondly, the Cr rich antiferromagnetic phase. The relationship between the decomposition of the B2 phase into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity is not well understood in these alloy systems and requires further detailed investigation.
